text.p: Canadian farmers estimate they will produce the following amounts of crops in the 1996/97 crop year, ending next July 31, according to a poll released on Monday by Statistics Canada.
In thousands of tonnes:
All Wheat 29,842 25,432
Spring Wheat 24,297 19,145
Durum Wheat 4,360 4,730
In thousands of tonnes:
Mixed grains 631 648
"Favorable weather conditions have more than compensated for the very late spring seeding of field crops, resulting in above-average yields," Statistics Canada said.

The Statistics Canada survey was conducted from July 26 to August 2. Grain analysts had said before the data was released that disease problems that have hit some Canadian grain and oilseed fields in recent weeks may not be reflected in the Statscan figures.

Statistics Canada said the forecast total wheat production of 1.097 billion bushels, if realized, would be the highest since 1992-93's 1.098 billion and compared with the record 1.179 billion in 1990-91.
It attributed the wheat improvement to higher yields and a 15 percent rise in seeded acreage.
"The driving force behind the increase in seeded acreage is high grain prices. High current and forecast prices are a direct result of tightening global supplies," the agency said.
For spring wheat, polled producers in Manitoba said they expect a 20 percent increase, Saskatchewan 38 percent and Alberta 15 percent.

Manitoba's spring wheat output was forecast to rise to 3.94 million tonnes from 3.27 million tonnes. Analysts said last week that fusarium head blight (scab) problems in Manitoba's Red River Valley did not surface until August and could have cost one million tonnes since the survey.
Drought-like conditions had already hit southwest Saskatchewan and southeast Alberta by the time of the survey.

Farmers in Ontario, the largest producer of winter wheat, are expecting much lower yields this year because of the harsh conditions of last winter as well as disease problems during the growing season, the agency said. Winter wheat remaining to be harvested in Ontario was expected to drop by 31 percent from last year. Canadian winter wheat output was forecast to fall to 1.18 million tonnes from 1.56 million tonnes.
The barley crop may be a record, due to an increase of 1.7 million seeded acres and yields at or above last year's.
It said the increase in seeded barley acreage -- to 13.18 million acres from 11.51 million -- was due to much higher prices and strong demand from the livestock sector.
Statscan said the 17 percent expected drop in canola output was due to a reduction in seeded acres to 9.15 million from 13.22 million, while yields were higher than last year.
"Industry sources claim that wheat is the preferred crop this year because of the relatively higher cost and risk factors involved in growing canola," the federal agency said.
It attributed the lower flaxseed production to a drop in seeded acres to 1.51 million from 2.17 million.
Spring wheat seeded acres rose to 25.92 million from 21.84 million, while durum dipped to 5.38 million from 5.40 million. Oats acreage rose to 5.09 million from 3.88 million.
